reviewMethod: Independent visual reading of all 32 question-paper pages and PDF pages 1–23 of the combined Ordinary Level scheme (cover, notes, the Paper 1 scale table on page 4, the slips note and printed summary of allocations on page 5, annotation palette, every Paper 1 model solution and marking note, and the Paper 2 title page). Each task boundary is the published scale, cross-checked against the printed summary.
sourceNotes: Candidates answer any five of Q1–6 (30 marks each) and any three of Q7–10 (50 marks each): 380 offered marks, 300 candidate marks. Every question is retained.
39 independently marked units, matching the printed summary of allocations on scheme page 5.

All 39 units were already authored, but three never shipped: Q2(c) was refused for naming lettered points without a decoded figure (the original page now supplies the Argand diagram), and Q3(a) and Q10(b)(iv) were refused because their joined credit-band text does not match the scheme text layer. Their marking points are now quoted line by line from the printed scheme. All existing IDs are kept; prompts are restored from the paper and topics corrected as metadata (complex numbers follow the Ordinary precedent of 3.1 Number systems).
The question booklet is LC003GLP100EV.pdf; its indexed scheme LC003GLP000EV.pdf is shared with Paper 2. All page references are PDF positions.

cards.stem: A farmer buys a new machine for €30 000. It depreciates (decreases in value) by 20% each year.
cards.questionText: (i) Find the value of the machine after 1 year. (ii) Hence, or otherwise, find the value of the machine after 2 years.
A farmer bought some livestock for €4716, including VAT. The cost of the livestock was €4500, excluding VAT. Calculate the percentage VAT rate used.
The farmer also bought land. One year later its value had increased by 12·5% and was now €52 875. Find the value of the land when the farmer bought it.

cards.stem: A ticket for a concert in Wales costs £59·50.
cards.questionText: (i) Using the exchange rate €1 = £0·85, find the cost of the concert ticket, in euro. (ii) Liam is a member of the venue’s Loyalty Club, so he gets a discount of 20% on all tickets. He buys 8 tickets for the concert. Work out the total cost of the 8 tickets, in euro.

Liam flies to the concert. He finds the following information: The aeroplane emits 28 000 grams of carbon per km, during the flight; His total flight distance is 394 km; There are 244 passengers on the flight. Work out the amount of carbon emitted during the flight, per passenger. Give your answer in kg, correct to 1 decimal place.

cards.stem: The number of people who will attend a concert (the attendance) can change depending on the price of a ticket. For a particular concert, this can be modelled by the function: A(x) = 17 600 − 160x, where A(x) is the attendance at the concert and x is the price of a ticket, in euro, with 0 ≤ x ≤ 110, x ∈ ℝ. Use the function A(x) to answer parts (c)(i) and (c)(ii).
cards.questionText: Find the attendance at this concert if the price of a ticket is €20.

cards.questionText: (i) Work out his net annual income. (ii) Hence, write his net annual income as a percentage of his gross annual income. Give your answer correct to the nearest percent.

cards.stem: An employee who works from home may qualify for tax relief on their electricity and broadband bills. The amount of tax relief such an employee can claim, A, is calculated using the formula: A = (Total annual electricity and broadband bills) × d/365 × 0·3, where d is the number of days worked from home.
cards.questionText: (i) Anne’s annual electricity bill was €1950 and broadband bill was €400. She worked from home for 120 days in the year. Find how much tax relief she can claim. Give your answer correct to the nearest cent. (ii) Tara also worked from home for a number of days. Tara’s total electricity and broadband bills were €2250. She claimed tax relief of €135 for working from home. Calculate how many days she worked from home.
